ip_top_stories.title: INF: Clarion expands Live Events as Taylor & Francis prepares for independence
ip_top_stories.summary: Taylor & Francis is preparing for independence as Informa moves to acquire events firm Clarion for £2.24 billion from Blackstone. The story signals significant structural shifts in the academic and professional publishing landscape.

ip_top_stories.title: Court Finds That Using Copyrighted Material as AI Training Data Is Not Fair Use
ip_top_stories.summary: A US court has ruled that using copyrighted material as AI training data does not qualify as fair use, delivering a significant legal blow to AI developers. The decision is likely to intensify ongoing litigation and policy debates around AI training practices.

ip_top_stories.title: Anthropic uses inquiry to claim current copyright law makes AI training "impossible"
ip_top_stories.summary: Anthropic has submitted evidence to an Australian government inquiry arguing that existing copyright law renders AI training effectively impossible. The claim is part of a broader push by AI companies to secure legislative carve-outs for training on copyrighted material.

ip_top_stories.title: EU considers copyright reform for gen-AI as US court rejects 'fair use' claim
ip_top_stories.summary: The European Union is consulting on potential copyright reforms in response to the rise of generative AI, with proposals that could include an opt-out right for rights holders. The move comes as a US court simultaneously rejected a fair use defence for AI training data, intensifying global regulatory pressure on AI developers.

ip_top_stories.title: ByteDance Fails to Escape YouTubers' AI Training, Copyright Suit
ip_top_stories.summary: A court has declined to dismiss a copyright lawsuit brought by YouTubers against ByteDance over the alleged use of their content for AI training. The ruling allows the case to proceed and adds to a growing body of AI training litigation against major technology companies.

ip_further_links.title: Malaysia May Let Creators Stop AI From Scraping Their Work Under Proposed Copyright Changes
ip_further_links.summary: Malaysia's intellectual property office is proposing copyright amendments that would give creators the right to opt out of having their works used for AI training.

ip_further_links.title: Meta Wins Pivotal AI Copyright Case, Despite Judge Calling Its Claims 'Nonsense'
ip_further_links.summary: Meta has won a significant AI copyright case, though the presiding judge was openly critical of some of the company's legal arguments during proceedings.

ip_further_links.title: Transformative Means More Than "Powered by AI"
ip_further_links.summary: A legal analysis argues that AI companies cannot claim transformative use simply by labelling their outputs as AI-generated, raising the bar for fair use defences in copyright disputes.

ip_further_links.title: Australia's ABC Rejects AI Copyright Opt-Out as Scraping Debate Intensifies
ip_further_links.summary: Australia's public broadcaster ABC has rejected proposals for an AI copyright opt-out regime, saying it believes its content has already been scraped without consent.

ip_further_links.title: Hong Kong puts AI copyright legislative amendments on hold, and pivots to establishing operational guidelines
ip_further_links.summary: Hong Kong has paused planned legislative changes to copyright law for AI and will instead focus on developing operational guidelines for AI use.

ip_further_links.title: Italy regulator probes AI music startup Suno over terms of service
ip_further_links.summary: Italy's data protection and competition regulator has opened a probe into AI music startup Suno, focusing on its terms of service and potential copyright implications.

ip_further_links.title: ARIA Boss Annabelle Herd Warns Australia Against Giving AI Giants a 'Free Ride'
ip_further_links.summary: The head of Australia's recording industry body has urged the government not to grant AI companies a copyright exemption for training, warning it would amount to a subsidy for large technology firms at creators' expense.

ip_further_links.title: OpenAI has 'work to do to rebuild trust' in Australia, executive tells AI inquiry
ip_further_links.summary: An OpenAI executive appearing before Australia's AI inquiry acknowledged the company needs to rebuild public trust, amid scrutiny over its data practices and copyright positions.

ip_further_links.title: Australian AI lab challenges case for copyright carve-out
ip_further_links.summary: An Australian AI research lab has submitted evidence to the government's AI inquiry pushing back against proposals for a broad copyright exemption for AI training.

ip_further_links.title: Events firm Informa to buy Clarion for £2.24 bil from Blackstone
ip_further_links.summary: Informa has announced a £2.24 billion deal to acquire events company Clarion from Blackstone, a transaction with implications for the broader publishing and media landscape.
